questions.q: Why does CROSS JOIN have no ON clause?
options: It doesn't try to match rows at all — it pairs every row with every row
ON is optional and simply omitted by convention
It's a syntax error to include ON with CROSS JOIN
CROSS JOIN uses WHERE instead of ON
questions.explain: CROSS JOIN produces the Cartesian product — there's no matching condition because every combination is included.

questions.q: If the left table has 504 rows and the right table has 4 rows, how many rows does CROSS JOIN return?
questions.explain: CROSS JOIN row counts multiply, not add — this is the single most important fact to remember about it.

questions.q: Why is an accidental CROSS JOIN considered a classic real-world bug?
options: Forgetting an ON clause on an intended INNER JOIN silently produces a huge Cartesian product instead of an error
CROSS JOIN always causes a syntax error, alerting the developer immediately
CROSS JOIN is deprecated and should never appear in any query
It only happens when joining more than five tables at once
questions.explain: No error is raised — the query just silently returns far more rows than intended, which can be a subtle and costly mistake.

questions.q: What is a legitimate use case for CROSS JOIN?
options: Generating every combination of two small sets, like every size paired with every color
Filtering rows based on a foreign key relationship
Sorting a single table by multiple columns
Removing duplicate rows from a result set
questions.explain: Building a full combination matrix (e.g. all size/color variant pairs) is one of the few intentional uses of CROSS JOIN.
